In the 2026-10-16T23:53:53Z harvest (run 38983767301, receipts in research/harvest-498cc7dd/) eight open Hotspawn CS2 fixtures came back with no pick at all: 1079170 BET-M vs Just Players, 1081126 Banda chuya vs Enjoy, 1081521 ex-6666 vs Privateer, 1081522 antidaun vs Phantom Academy, 1081527 aimclub vs BASEMENT BOYS, 1081532 ASTRAL vs Leo, 1081861 Lynn Vision vs Morningstar and 1081863 Chinggis Warriors vs WXM. Root cause, evidenced in that run's own logs: HLTV answered HTTP 403 to that runner for https://www.hltv.org/matches while every other source in the same run answered 200, and the identical read at 19:57Z the same evening answered 200. Sources.get treated that 403 as a permanent access restriction and blocked the host for the rest of the run, removing (a) the HLTV lineups scripts/vrs.py::identify() uses to choose between the two rosters Valve lists under one label and (b) the ranking-order research pick. Fixed in scripts/refresh.py: a rate-limited 403/429 is now waited out on the identical URL with identical headers (Retry-After honoured, then 10s/30s/60s, 120s cap) and only blocked if it keeps refusing; 401, 404 and region/challenge pages are unchanged. This is a pipeline-risk finding, not a coverage gap: the snapshot this site publishes (data/latest.json, generated 2026-10-16T19:59:25Z) reached HLTV with a 200 and carries a pick for all 21 open rows, so nothing published is affected. The recovered row count is deliberately not claimed here; it is confirmed by the next scheduled refresh.

status: Recorded discrepancy — the board uses the earlier, conservative value, and this does not block publication
finding: Hotspawn describes its lock in two different places. The official how-it-works page says 'Your picks lock 5 minutes before the scheduled start time of the relevant match or game', while every CS2 row of its fixtures API read on 17 October 2026 at 00:50Z carries lock_offset_sec 360, i.e. six minutes before the scheduled start (the same value appears on every row of the page, so it is a feed-wide offset rather than a single odd row). This project derives the lock shown on each card from the API's own per-fixture lock_time, which is the earlier of the two by one minute and therefore the conservative choice: a pick is withheld at the API lock, never later. The discrepancy is published here rather than smoothed over, and it is not treated as a source failure.

status: Needs review — repository setting change required (owner action) (integrated into the arena/03befae8-maltaproj4 branch, session 03befae8)
finding: Two publishers write to the same Pages site and the site shows whichever deployed last. The repository's Pages source is still the legacy branch build (`main:/`, read from the Pages API on 2026-10-17), so every merge to `main` also triggers a legacy rebuild of the committed root fallback, while the verified workflow publishes the refreshed artifact. Measured on 2026-10-17: at ~00:33 UTC the live `build-info.json` was the verified artifact revision `9029e8f1abcc4459bc1efe73638b8b7fcfb19735`, built 00:15:28Z, 96 rows, snapshot 00:15:28Z, 29 of 34 open fixtures priced; at ~00:37 UTC the same URL served revision `b13968ebe6fa6f308c3accc60780640d553d43ba`, built 00:27:40Z, 83 rows, snapshot 16 Oct 19:59:25Z, 17 of 21 open fixtures priced — the root fallback that merge `0d77fe9` (PR #55) refreshed and the legacy build then published. Nothing is invented in either build and each is internally consistent; the defect is that the fallback can only ever hold the snapshot committed at staging time, so a merge can leave the public site on older data until the next verified publish. The freshness gate compares the live receipt with the commit being deployed (revision and a 60-minute snapshot budget) and re-publishes when either fails, and four scheduled slots an hour exist for exactly that, so the site converges again without intervention. This session tried the one-line fix — `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages` with `build_type=workflow` — and the GitHub token available here returned 403 'Resource not accessible by integration'. Owner action, one step: repository Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source → GitHub Actions, after which the verified artifact is the only publisher and the root fallback stops being served. Until then the fallback stays in the repository, staged after build and validation, and every stale window is visible in the receipt above rather than hidden.

status: Measured — the live site lagged the publish by ~26 minutes while every publish run was green; legacy Pages builds are soft-limited to 10 per hour
finding: While checking that its own merge reached visitors, session b06ee902 found the live deployment frozen at build-info built_at 2026-10-25T14:59:26Z while main's committed root already carried 15:00:47Z and later. The Pages build list explains it: 15:04:50 errored fd4ba08, 15:13:19 errored e379ee6, 15:20:18 errored 9cef2fb ('Page build failed.'), then 15:20:53 built f07cfc6, after which the live build-info advanced to 15:25:24Z with 75 rows. The site content was not the cause and was ruled out by diff: the last successful build before the burst (57d34f2, committed 15:02:17Z) and the first failing one (fd4ba08, 15:04:49Z) differ in exactly one file, COORDINATION.md, and the tree is 120 MB across 2,561 files with no symlinks, so neither the 1 GB site limit nor the 100 MB per-file limit is in play. GitHub documents the actual constraint: 'GitHub Pages sites have a soft limit of 10 builds per hour. This limit does not apply if you build and publish your site with a custom GitHub Actions workflow.' This repository is published with build_type legacy and main receives commits every few minutes from many concurrent sessions, so builds exceed that soft limit and the served site stays on the last successful deployment until a slot frees. Nothing is broken and no pick is wrong: the board is simply older than the repository during a burst, and a visitor reads an older snapshot than the run that just succeeded. The remedy (switching Pages to a GitHub Actions deployment) is a repository-settings change outside this session's file scope, so it is recorded here for the owner rather than applied unilaterally while other sessions publish through the legacy main:/ root fallback.
impact: Presentation and freshness only: no pick, price or probability changes, and the site recovers on its own once a build slot frees (observed 14:59Z to 15:25Z). It does mean that 'the publish run was green' is not by itself evidence that the served page is current; the deployed build-info.json must be compared with the committed root, with a cache-busting query because the CDN otherwise serves the previous build-info.json.
